title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Properly Carrying Out Adjudication Work in Accordance with Law During Emergency Rescue and Recovery Reconstruction in Zhouqu, Gansu and Other Areas and Effectively Maintaining Social Stability in Disaster-Stricken Areas
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Lawfully Conducting Trial Work during Rescue, Relief, and Post-Disaster Reconstruction in Zhouqu, Gansu Province, and Other Areas, and Effectively Maintaining Social Stability in Disaster-Affected Areas

Fa [2010] No. 271

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Recently, catastrophic mountain torrent and mudslide disasters occurred in Zhouqu, Gansu Province, and other areas, causing enormous losses to the lives and property of the people in the disaster-affected areas and severe damage to production and living in those areas. Under the strong leadership and meticulous planning of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council, rescue and relief efforts have achieved phased results, and post-disaster reconstruction work is about to commence. During the period of rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction, all people's courts at all levels nationwide shall, under the leadership of the Party and based on maintaining social stability, resolving conflicts, and promoting harmony, provide strong judicial guarantees and services for rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction, ensuring the comprehensive victory of rescue and relief efforts and the smooth progress of post-disaster reconstruction. To properly conduct relevant trial work and effectively maintain social stability in the disaster-affected areas, the following matters are hereby notified:

1. People's courts at all levels shall deeply understand the series of decisions and deployments made by the Central Committee of the CPC and the State Council regarding rescue and relief work, as well as the important instructions of General Secretary Hu Jintao, and continue to regard rescue and relief as the most urgent and important task at present. From the overall situation, and from the perspectives of being conducive to maintaining social stability, safeguarding the fundamental interests of the broad masses, strengthening national unity, consolidating the achievements of rescue and relief, and ensuring the smooth progress of post-disaster reconstruction, they shall conscientiously conduct the trial and enforcement of cases involving the catastrophic mountain torrent and mudslide disasters in Zhouqu, Gansu Province, and other areas. They shall diligently study and accurately apply the relevant laws, administrative regulations, and judicial interpretations for handling disaster-related cases, including the Emergency Response Law of the People's Republic of China and the Flood Control Regulations of the People's Republic of China, and in light of the actual circumstances of the current rescue and relief work, strengthen overall coordination to provide strong judicial guarantees for rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction, effectively maintain public order in the disaster-affected areas, and enhance the sense of security among the people in those areas.

2. All criminal activities that harm rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction shall be severely punished according to law, and social stability in the disaster-affected areas shall be resolutely maintained. People's courts shall, according to law, protect the safety of life and property of the people in disaster-affected areas, and severely crack down on illegal and criminal acts that involve meddling in conflicts and creating incidents, intentionally undermining stability in disaster-affected areas, damaging the achievements of rescue and relief, impeding the smooth progress of post-disaster reconstruction, or affecting the confidence and determination of the people in disaster-affected areas to rebuild their homes.

Adhere to the policy of handling cases that endanger social stability in disaster-affected areas under special circumstances in a special manner. For criminal acts that seriously harm rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction, they shall be tried and adjudicated quickly within the statutory time limit, striving to enable the people in disaster-affected areas to feel the determination and strength of the people's courts in maintaining stability and combating crime in the shortest possible time, deterring potential criminals, and preventing and reducing the occurrence of crime.

Strictly implement the criminal policy of combining leniency with severity, distinguish between illegal and criminal acts of different natures, demonstrate judicial authority, and provide strong judicial guarantees for production and living in disaster-affected areas in a manner visible and perceptible to the people.

3. The following criminal acts occurring during the period of rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction shall be given heavier punishment according to law:

(1) Theft, robbery, forcible seizure, intentional destruction of materials, equipment, or facilities used for rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction; fraud or extortion of money under the pretext of disaster relief fundraising; and trafficking of orphaned, disabled, or elderly children or women in disaster-affected areas.

(2) Illegal business operations, forced transactions, or other acts that seriously disrupt market order in disaster-affected areas and affect the normal production and living of the people in those areas for the purpose of seeking exorbitant profits.

(3) Intentional fabrication, dissemination, or distribution of false or terroristic information that is detrimental to stability in disaster-affected areas, affecting and endangering social stability.

(4) Acts such as obstructing public administration, assembling a crowd to disturb social order, public place order, traffic order, or storming state organs, which seriously affect the progress of rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction.

(5) Production or sale of substandard products, poisonous or harmful food, fake or inferior drugs in disaster-affected areas, or intentional provision of such goods to disaster-affected areas under the pretext of disaster relief.

(6) Embezzlement or misappropriation of post-disaster reconstruction funds or materials; abuse of power or dereliction of duty that harms the smooth progress of rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction, and seriously damages the image of the Party and the state.

(7) Destruction of public facilities such as power, transportation, or communication facilities.

(8) Acts that hinder the prevention and control of infectious diseases or other acts endangering public health.

4. Research on litigation issues that may arise due to the flood disaster shall be strengthened, normal trial work order shall be restored as soon as possible, and a "green channel" for disaster-related cases shall be opened and kept unimpeded. During trial and enforcement, special attention shall be paid to protecting the legitimate civil rights and interests of minors, the elderly living alone, and persons disabled by the disaster in the disaster-affected areas. Enforcement measures shall be used with caution; in particular, property preservation measures such as sealing up, distraining, freezing, or transferring and enforcement measures shall not be taken against funds and materials explicitly designated for rescue and relief. Proactive measures to facilitate and benefit the people shall be taken, judicial aid shall be increased, and the scope of judicial aid to the people in disaster-affected areas shall be expanded.

5. People's courts in disaster-affected areas shall, together with relevant departments, conduct comprehensive investigations and promptly resolve conflicts and disputes arising during rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction. They shall actively support and assist relevant departments in carrying out resettlement, consolation, subsidies, relief, and other work. For conflicts and disputes arising during rescue and disaster relief work, people's courts shall proactively study them from a legal perspective and proactively put forward suggestions and countermeasures on how to administer according to law and resolve disputes.

6. People's courts in disaster-affected areas shall further implement the work principle of "mediation priority, combination of mediation and adjudication," treat mediation as the primary option for handling cases, consciously and proactively use mediation to resolve conflicts and disputes, promote social harmony and stability, achieve case closure, matter resolution, and harmony among parties, and effectively maintain a good situation of harmony and stability in disaster-affected areas. In particular, they shall firmly rely on the leadership of the local Party committee, actively seek government support, encourage participation from all sectors of society, and rely on the "grand mediation" work system of people's mediation, administrative mediation, and judicial mediation to form a strong joint force for resolving conflicts and disputes, promptly resolving social conflicts and disputes at the grassroots level and in their nascent stages, and effectively promoting social harmony and stability in disaster-affected areas.

7. During the post-disaster reconstruction period, if a party brings a case to a people's court, and the case meets the conditions for acceptance, the court shall promptly file the case and effectively guarantee the realization of the party's right of action. If disaster victims who have been relocated to other places or have gone to relatives bring disputes to the people's court, due to changes in the parties' places of residence, in matters of jurisdiction, the high people's courts shall, in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law and other relevant legal provisions, and based on the principles of convenience for disaster victims and benefit to stability, make overall arrangements. For disputes that fall within the scope of case acceptance of the people's court, the people's court shall effectively strengthen litigation guidance and legal clarification for civil cases involving the disaster, and pay attention to providing litigation risk warnings to the parties; for disputes that are not within or are not suitable for handling by the people's court, the court shall conscientiously guide the masses in their thinking and lead the parties to choose other means to resolve the disputes.

8. If a party is unable to timely assert its rights due to force majeure factors such as catastrophic mountain torrent and mudslide disasters, the statute of limitations shall be suspended in accordance with the provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law, and the limitation period shall continue to run from the date when the cause of suspension is eliminated. If a party is unable to participate in litigation activities due to rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction, the people's court shall, according to law, postpone or suspend the trial; after the cause of postponement or suspension is eliminated, the trial shall be promptly resumed.

9. For cases filed by persons who have gone missing due to catastrophic mountain torrent and mudslide disasters to apply for declaration of disappearance or declaration of death, the people's court shall, according to law, actively accept the cases in order to clarify personal status and property relations as soon as possible.

10. During the period of rescue, relief, and post-disaster reconstruction, combined with the trial work of related cases, legal publicity and education shall be strengthened, psychological comfort and thought guidance shall be patiently provided to the people in disaster-affected areas, especially the families of the deceased, and assistance shall be given in resettling the people in disaster-affected areas.

11. People's courts in disaster-affected areas shall fully implement various measures such as personnel prevention, material prevention, and technical prevention, vigorously strengthen the security and protection of the people's court, effectively protect the life and property safety of the litigants involved, effectively protect the life and property safety of judges and court staff and their families, and effectively protect the safety of court archives, case files, infrastructure, and other trial resources in disaster-affected areas.

12. For cases involving mudslide disasters, the people's court may refer to the Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Handling of Cases Related to the Wenchuan Earthquake (I)", the Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Handling of Cases Related to the Wenchuan Earthquake (II)", and the Supreme People's Court's "Notice on Lawfully Conducting Trial Work during Earthquake Relief and Post-Disaster Reconstruction in Yushu, Qinghai Province, and Effectively Maintaining Social Stability in Disaster-Affected Areas" for handling. If new issues concerning the application of law arise in trial work, the matter shall be promptly reported to the higher people's court, and major issues concerning the application of law shall be promptly reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court.

So notified.

August 26, 2010
